hero.title: Hi, I'm Mert. I work on security and the infrastructure underneath it.
hero.valueProposition: I'm an Erasmus Mundus scholar in the CyberMACS master's programme in applied cybersecurity. Before that I ran the network and servers at Kadir Has University's cybersecurity center, and I still build data platforms for research projects. Lately I've been working on anomaly detection in power grids, OSINT for SCADA systems and EEG-based brain–computer interfaces.

philosophy.title: About me
content: Most of my work sits where security meets day-to-day operations: keeping a lab's machines and network running, digging through memory dumps for malware that never touches the disk, and turning messy research data into something people can actually query. I like systems that are simple enough to understand when they break.

I'm also a search and rescue operator and instructor at AFAD. Rescue work teaches you to keep plans simple, to check your gear before you need it and to stay calm when things go wrong. I try to bring the same habits to the servers I look after.

timeline.description: Full EU scholarship. The first year is at Kadir Has University in Istanbul and SRH Berlin, the second at UKIM in Skopje. Courses in cryptography, network security and applied cybersecurity.
Research on EEG-based brain–computer interfaces. I also teach the lab sessions of undergraduate MIS courses on algorithms and operating systems.
Ran the network and servers of the Center for Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection, and kept the GPU machines going for the lab's machine learning projects.
Urban and mountain search and rescue under AFAD and INSARAG standards. As a certified AFAD instructor I also teach disaster preparedness and USAR courses.

contact.title: Contact
contact.description: If you're working on something in security, infrastructure or research data and want to talk, send me an email.
